subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy layer, or should cron inherit an existing policy such as `tools.subagents.tools`?
rationale: This changes a security-sensitive public config surface and policy precedence across cron delivery, per-job `toolsAllow`, and backend-specific enforcement, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and tests for embedded and CLI-backed cron behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron runs as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling two different execution concepts.

options.title: Keep per-job toolsAllow only
options.body: Avoid a new global config surface but leave operators without a hard cron-wide deny for tools such as `message`.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and tests for embedded and CLI-backed cron behavior.
